concept.name: Artifact Registry Versioning

relationships.description: Connects Artifact Registry Versioning to canary deployments in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Artifact registry versioning pairs human-readable semantic tags (`v1.4.2`) with immutable content-addressed digests (`sha256:...`), ensuring every build, deployment, and rollback runs the exact verified bytes.
spark.keyTakeaway: Tag for humans, deploy by immutable digest: mutable tags like `:latest` or `:v1` can be overwritten silently, whereas `image@sha256:...` guarantees bit-for-bit reproducibility.

concept.whyItMatters: Overwriting a mutable tag like `:latest` or `:prod` breaks Kubernetes pod autoscaling—existing pods run old bytes while newly scheduled pods pull different bytes under the same tag. Content-addressed OCI registries (AWS ECR, Google Artifact Registry, Harbor, GHCR) store layers by SHA-256 digest and support tag immutability, SBOM attachment, and Cosign cryptographic signatures.
whenToUse: Production container, Helm chart, or library pipelines (Maven, PyPI, npm) where deployments and rollbacks must be 100% deterministic.
Regulated software supply chains requiring SLSA provenance, SBOMs, and Cosign signature verification via admission controllers (Kyverno/OPA) before pods start.
Multi-architecture builds (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`) unified under a single OCI Image Index (manifest list) digest.
whenNotToUse: Local `docker compose` development loops where fast iteration with a local `:dev` tag is convenient and never leaves your laptop.
Storing multi-gigabyte raw ML training datasets or unstructured blobs—use object storage (S3/GCS) with DVC or LakeFS instead of an OCI registry.
keyPoints: Tag vs. Digest: a tag (`v2.3.1`) is a mutable pointer; a digest (`sha256:9f86...`) is the cryptographic hash of the OCI manifest JSON, which in turn hashes every layer.
Enable tag immutability at the repository level (`IMMUTABLE` in AWS ECR / GAR) so no CI job can overwrite a released `vX.Y.Z` tag.
OCI Artifacts beyond containers: Helm charts, Wasm modules, SBOMs (SPDX/CycloneDX), and Cosign `.sig` attestations all live in the same OCI Distribution Spec registry.

Semantic Versioning (SemVer `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) communicates API compatibility for libraries/Helm charts, while Git SHA + timestamp tags (`v1.4.2-g8a3f1c`) give exact commit traceability for app images.

Lifecycle & retention policies: unreferenced digests and PR-preview tags explode storage bills; automate cleanup rules that keep the last $N$ prod tags while purging untagged manifests after 7–14 days.

examples.title: Pinning Production Pods by Immutable OCI Digest
examples.scenario: A deployment manifest specifies `ghcr.io/acme/api:v1.8.0` without a digest, and a hotfix accidentally re-pushes `v1.8.0`.
examples.outcome: Switching the CI pipeline to resolve and commit `ghcr.io/acme/api:v1.8.0@sha256:4b22...` guarantees every node across all availability zones pulls identical verified layers.

examples.title: Multi-Arch Image Index + Cosign Signature Verification
examples.scenario: A platform runs both x86_64 and AWS Graviton (arm64) nodes and must block unsigned images.
examples.outcome: Buildx pushes an OCI Image Index manifest referencing both arch digests, `cosign sign` attaches a `.sig` OCI referrer, and Kyverno verifies the signature against the digest at pod admission.

tradeOffs.factor: Immutable Tags + Digests vs. Mutable Environment Tags (`:staging`, `:prod`)
tradeOffs.pro: Immutable tags + digests prevent silent drift, cache poisoning, and broken rollbacks.
tradeOffs.con: Requires updating GitOps manifests with new tags/digests on every release instead of re-tagging in place.

tradeOffs.factor: Single Registry with Promotion vs. Separate Dev/Prod Registries
tradeOffs.pro: Separate prod registries isolate blast radius, enforce stricter IAM, and simplify retention rules.
tradeOffs.con: Requires cross-registry replication (`crane copy` or ECR replication) to preserve digests.

tradeOffs.factor: Aggressive Retention Policies vs. Long-Term Audit Archival
tradeOffs.pro: Expiring PR/dev images after 14 days cuts registry storage costs by 60–80%.
tradeOffs.con: Deleting old prod tags breaks `kubectl rollout undo` or autoscaling if a running pod's digest is purged.

failureModes.name: Tag Overwrite / Split-Brain Autoscaling
failureModes.description: A CI job overwrites `:prod` with new code; existing pods run old code while HPA-scaled pods pull new code under the same tag.
failureModes.mitigation: Enable repository-level tag immutability and deploy strictly via `@sha256:...` digests.

failureModes.name: Purging Active Production Digests
failureModes.description: An aggressive cleanup policy (`keep last 10 images`) deletes an older image still referenced by a long-running Kubernetes Deployment, causing `ImagePullBackOff` on node scale-up.
failureModes.mitigation: Protect release tags (`v*`) from auto-expiry, or query active cluster digests before running registry garbage collection.

failureModes.name: Floating Base Image Drift
failureModes.description: A Dockerfile starts with `FROM python:3.12-slim` without a digest; rebuilding the exact same Git commit a week later pulls a different OS/OpenSSL layer.
failureModes.mitigation: Pin base images by digest (`FROM python:3.12-slim@sha256:...`) and automate bumps via Renovate or Dependabot.

failureModes.name: Orphaned Multi-Arch Child Manifests
failureModes.description: Garbage collection deletes individual `amd64`/`arm64` child manifests if retention rules only match the parent Image Index tag.
failureModes.mitigation: Use OCI-aware registries (ECR, GAR, Harbor v2.8+) that trace manifest-list references during garbage collection.

commonMistakes: Deploying `:latest` or `:main` to staging/production Kubernetes clusters.
Leaving tag mutability enabled on production repositories, allowing accidental `docker push` overwrites.
Rebuilding artifacts per environment (dev -> staging -> prod) instead of building once, testing, and promoting the exact same SHA-256 digest.
Ignoring `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` hazards with mutable tags—nodes cache stale layers while other nodes pull new ones.
Forgetting to include `cosign` signatures and SBOMs when copying/promoting images between registries (use `cosign copy` or `crane`).

sections.content:
## The idea

An artifact registry is a content-addressable storage system. Every container image, Helm chart, or language package you push is decomposed into compressed blobs and a JSON manifest whose SHA-256 hash—the **digest**—uniquely identifies that exact byte sequence. **Tags** (`v1.4.2`, `latest`) are merely human-friendly aliases pointing to a digest. Reliable delivery pipelines separate human naming (immutable SemVer or commit-SHA tags) from machine execution (pinning `@sha256:...` digests).

## Concrete walkthrough

Follow a single build from commit `8a3f1c` to production Kubernetes:

1. **Build & Push Once**: CI runs `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64` and pushes `gar.dev/acme/orders:1.4.2-8a3f1c` to a staging repository with tag immutability enabled.
2. **Capture Digest & Attest**: The registry returns the OCI Image Index digest `sha256:7c9e...`. CI runs Trivy vulnerability scanning, generates a CycloneDX SBOM, and executes `cosign sign` to attach the signature and SBOM as OCI referrers to `sha256:7c9e...`.
3. **Promote Without Rebuilding**: After integration tests pass, CI runs `crane copy` (or `cosign copy`) to promote `sha256:7c9e...` and its attached signatures to the `prod` registry—zero rebuilds, zero `apt-get` drift.
4. **Verify & Run**: Argo CD updates the Deployment to `prod-gar.dev/acme/orders:1.4.2@sha256:7c9e...`, and Kyverno verifies the Cosign signature before the kubelet pulls the layers.

sections.content:
## Tagging schemes across ecosystems

Different artifact types call for different versioning contracts:

- **Application Containers**: Use `<semver>-<git_sha>` (e.g., `2.1.0-9b4e2a1`) or CalVer (`2026.11.12-9b4e2a1`) paired with `@sha256:...` in deployment manifests. Never reuse a tag.
- **Shared Libraries (npm, PyPI, Maven)**: Strictly follow **SemVer 2.0** (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) because downstream `package.json` or `pom.xml` resolvers use range constraints (`^1.4.0`).
- **Helm Charts (OCI)**: Store charts in OCI registries (`oci://ghcr.io/acme/charts/api:1.4.2`) with independent chart `version` (packaging changes) and `appVersion` (workload version).

## Versioning & promotion strategies compared

| Strategy | Mutability | Rollback Safety | Storage Growth | Best Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`:latest` / `:prod` Tag** | Mutable | Unsafe (old bytes lost) | Low | Local dev only |
| **SemVer Tag (`v1.4.2`)** | Immutable (enforced) | Safe if repo blocks overwrite | Medium | Libraries, Helm charts, releases |
| **Git SHA Tag (`g8a3f1c`)** | Immutable | Safe + commit-traceable | High (needs GC) | Continuous deployment apps |
| **Tag + `@sha256` Digest** | Cryptographically immutable | Guaranteed bit-for-bit | High (needs GC) | Production K8s & regulated workloads |

## Failure modes

1. **Silent Re-Tagging Corruption**: Without registry immutability, two concurrent CI runs on the same branch overwrite each other's tags. Fix: turn on `IMMUTABLE` tag enforcement in ECR/GAR/Harbor.
2. **Base-Image Supply Chain Drift**: Using `FROM node:20-alpine` pulls different packages on Monday vs. Friday. Fix: pin base images to `@sha256:...` digests.
3. **Broken Rollbacks After GC**: A 30-day retention rule deletes the previous release's image while a canary fails. Fix: exempt `v*` release tags and any digest currently running in production clusters.
4. **Missing Signatures After Promotion**: `docker pull` + `docker push` strips OCI referrer signatures and changes manifest digests if re-compressed. Fix: use `crane copy` or `cosign copy` to preserve exact manifests and attestations.

## Lifecycle and cost governance

Unchecked CI pipelines generate terabytes of ephemeral PR-preview images. Separate registries or tag prefixes into two tiers: **ephemeral** (`pr-*`, `dev-*`, purged after 7–14 days) and **release** (`v*`, retained for 180–365 days or protected by an active-cluster-digest check). Combine this with multi-stage Docker builds (`distroless` or `alpine`) to shrink per-image layer footprints from ~900 MB to <50 MB.

## Practical checklist

- **Enable tag immutability** on all staging and production OCI repositories.
- **Deploy by `@sha256` digest** in Kubernetes/GitOps manifests, keeping the human tag as a prefix (`api:v1.4.2@sha256:...`).
- **Pin base images** in every `Dockerfile` using `@sha256:...` and automate updates with Renovate.
- **Build once, promote via `crane`/`cosign copy`**: never re-run `docker build` per environment.
- **Automate tiered retention**: expire untagged manifests in 7 days and `pr-*` tags in 14 days while protecting active production digests.

interviewProblems.title: Artifact Registry Versioning
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Artifact Registry Versioning. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Artifact registry versioning pairs human-readable semantic tags (`v1.4.2`) with immutable content-addressed digests (`sha256:...`), ensuring every build, deployment, and rollback runs the exact verified bytes.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Prod OCI Registry applies the primary invariant and coordinates with K8s Admission + Kubelet.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, K8s Admission + Kubelet experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Enable repository-level tag immutability and deploy strictly via `@sha256:...` digests.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Tag for humans, deploy by immutable digest: mutable tags like `:latest` or `:v1` can be overwritten silently, whereas `image@sha256:...` guarantees bit-for-bit reproducibility.
Avoid trap: Deploying `:latest` or `:main` to staging/production Kubernetes clusters.
Avoid trap: Leaving tag mutability enabled on production repositories, allowing accidental `docker push` overwrites.
When to reach for it: Production container, Helm chart, or library pipelines (Maven, PyPI, npm) where deployments and rollbacks must be 100% deterministic.
When to reach for it: Regulated software supply chains requiring SLSA provenance, SBOMs, and Cosign signature verification via admission controllers (Kyverno/OPA) before pods start.
